may_be_looking_for: have a diagnosis of definite systemic lupus (which may be associated with secondary conditions like antiphospholipid syndrome or Sjögren's)
are newly diagnosed or have known lupus that is untreated or in relapse
are considered stable by their doctor
need blood tests as part of their follow-up
may_exclude_people_who: have a main autoimmune disease other than lupus
are under legal protection, guardianship, or curatorship
do not consent to data processing
patient_summary: This study is looking at how certain receptors on immune cells (Natural Killer T cells and monocytes) change in people with active or newly diagnosed lupus compared to those with inactive lupus. The researchers are focusing on a receptor called neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) and other Fc gamma receptors.
patient_title: Studying immune cell receptors in lupus patients
questions_to_ask_clinician: What are the criteria used to define active or inactive lupus for this study?
Will my diagnosis of secondary conditions (e.g., antiphospholipid syndrome) affect my eligibility?
How is the stability of lupus determined?
What does participation involve beyond the blood sample?
uncertainty_notes: This study is observational and involves only a blood sample. It does not test a new treatment.
The study is currently recruiting participants in France.
The study is not a treatment trial, so it does not offer any direct therapeutic benefit.
what_researchers_are_studying: The researchers want to understand the role of the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) in Natural Killer T cells (iNKT) and monocytes, and the surface expression of Fc gamma type II and III receptors in lupus patients. They are comparing these markers between patients with active or newly diagnosed lupus and those with inactive lupus.
